description: Machine-readable contract for formulation intake, provisional classification, Indian patent/TK screening, biological diversity (ABS) flags, and safe expert referral.

intake_fields.missing_prompt: Please specify the primary intended purpose: Is the product meant to treat/prevent a disease, serve as a daily dietary food supplement, or provide external cosmetic care?
Please confirm the source of active ingredients: Are all botanical/mineral ingredients documented in First Schedule authoritative Ayurvedic texts?

Please specify the authoritative book listed in the First Schedule to the Drugs and Cosmetics Act from which this exact classical recipe is derived. (Note: Missing book reference requires clarification and cannot be assumed proprietary).
Is the formulation prepared strictly according to an unchanged recipe from an authoritative Ayurvedic book, or is it a proprietary combination or modified dosage form?
What is the intended route of administration (e.g. oral, topical)? Note: Injectable/parenteral administration is strictly prohibited for Ayurvedic medicines and Ayurveda Aahara.
Is the product a purified, standardized fraction characterized by at least four bioactive or phytochemical markers?
Is the recipe or ingredient described in authoritative Ayurvedic books listed in Schedule A of the Ayurveda Aahara Regulations 2022?
Does the product labelling or advertising make any claims to prevent, treat, mitigate, or cure any human disease or disorder? (Prohibited under Regulation 8 of Ayurveda Aahara Regulations).
Are any synthetic vitamins, minerals, amino acids, or isolated chemical additives added to the formulation? (Prohibited under Regulation 3(4) of Ayurveda Aahara Regulations).
Does the formulation utilize biological resources (plants, microbes, animals) or associated traditional knowledge accessed from India?

What is the legal status of the applicant? (Section 3(2) foreign entities require NBA approval before grant under s. 6(1); Section 7 domestic entities require registration before grant and approval at commercialization under s. 6(2)).
Is the applicant intending to apply for a patent in India or internationally for this formulation?
Does the applicant possess comparative experimental data demonstrating an unexpected synergistic technical effect exceeding mere aggregation of component properties?

rules.name: Classical Ayurvedic Medicine
rules.condition: intended_use == 'medicinal' and ingredients_classical_status == 'all_classical' and formulation_source == 'exact_classical_recipe' and classical_book_citation != null and administration_route != 'parenteral'

outcome.legal_basis: Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 Section 3(a) read with First Schedule; Drugs Rules, 1945 Rule 158-B(I)
outcome.missing_citation_fallback: If authoritative text citation is missing, system halts confident routing and triggers RULE-UNC-01 for clarification; missing evidence must NEVER demote to proprietary.

rules.name: Patent or Proprietary Ayurvedic Medicine
rules.condition: intended_use == 'medicinal' and ingredients_classical_status == 'all_classical' and formulation_source in ['proprietary_combination', 'modified_dosage_form'] and administration_route != 'parenteral'

outcome.legal_basis: Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 Section 3(h); Drugs Rules, 1945 Rule 158-B(II)
outcome.evidentiary_requirement: Published scientific literature or safety/efficacy data under Rule 158-B(II)

rules.name: Novel / Non-Classical Formulation Referral
rules.condition: intended_use == 'medicinal' and (ingredients_classical_status in ['partial_classical', 'synthetic_added'] or formulation_source == 'novel_unlisted') and not phytopharmaceutical_criteria

outcome.non_forcing_notice: Product contains synthetic substances or botanicals outside First Schedule classical ASU texts. Cannot be classified under standard AYUSH licensing.
outcome.legal_basis: Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 non-ASU provisions; New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019

rules.name: Phytopharmaceutical Drug Referral
rules.condition: intended_use == 'medicinal' and phytopharmaceutical_criteria == true and administration_route != 'parenteral'

outcome.non_forcing_notice: Standardized fraction with >=4 bioactives falls under CDSCO modern drug regulatory framework, not state AYUSH licensing.
outcome.legal_basis: Drugs Rules, 1945 Rule 2(eb), Rule 122E, Schedule Y Appendix I/IA; CDSCO Guidance Document 2018

rules.name: Ayurveda Aahara Food
rules.condition: intended_use == 'food_dietary' and food_authoritative_text == true and disease_cure_claims == false and synthetic_nutrients_added == false and administration_route != 'parenteral'

outcome.licensing_authority: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)
outcome.legal_basis: Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahara) Regulations, 2022 Regulation 2(b) (definition/exclusions), Regulation 3(4) (synthetic nutrients ban), Regulation 8 (disease claims prohibition), Regulation 13(a) (front-of-pack logo); Schedule A

rules.name: Ayurvedic Cosmetic
rules.condition: intended_use == 'cosmetic' and administration_route == 'topical' and disease_cure_claims == false

rules.name: Section 3(p) Traditional Knowledge Exclusion
rules.condition: patent_filing_intended == true and ingredients_classical_status == 'all_classical' and formulation_source == 'exact_classical_recipe'

outcome.legal_basis: The Patents Act, 1970 Section 3(p); CGPDTM Examination Guidelines (2012) Paragraph 4.1
outcome.explanation: Inventions that are in effect traditional knowledge or aggregation of known properties of traditionally known components are non-patentable.

rules.name: Section 3(e) Mere Admixture vs Synergism
rules.condition: patent_filing_intended == true and formulation_source in ['proprietary_combination', 'modified_dosage_form'] and not synergistic_data_available

outcome.statutory_risk: Rejection under Section 3(e) as mere admixture
outcome.legal_basis: The Patents Act, 1970 Section 3(e); CGPDTM Guidelines (2012) Paragraph 4.1
outcome.explanation: Mere aggregation of properties of components is excluded. Synergistic effect must be proven with comparative experimental data.

outcome.legal_basis: The Patents Act, 1970 Section 10(4)(d)(ii); Patents Rules, 2003 Rule 13
outcome.explanation: Patent applicant must disclose the source and geographical origin of the biological material in the patent specification.

rules.name: NBA Section 6 Approval and Registration Mandates (Amended 2023)

outcome.legal_basis: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 Section 6(1) and Section 6(2) as amended by Act 10 of 2023; Biological Diversity Rules, 2024 Rule 14 read with 2025 Amendment Rules
outcome.mandate_details: Under amended Section 6: Section 3(2) foreign entities must obtain NBA approval before grant of IPR under s. 6(1); Section 7 domestic Indian entities must register with the NBA before grant of IPR and obtain NBA approval prior to commercialization under s. 6(2). Practitioner exemptions under s. 6(1A) do not waive IPR registration or approval.

outcome.legal_basis: Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 Section 3(h); FSSAI Ayurveda Aahara Regulations, 2022 Regulation 2(b)
outcome.explanation: Injectable/parenteral formulations cannot be licensed as Ayurvedic medicines or Ayurveda Aahara under Indian law.

rules.name: Disease Cure Claims in Food or Cosmetic

outcome.legal_basis: FSSAI Ayurveda Aahara Regulations, 2022 Regulation 8; Drugs and Magic Remedies Act, 1954 Sections 3 and 4; FSSAI Advertising and Claims Regulations 2018 Regulation 4
outcome.explanation: Products claiming disease prevention or cure cannot be licensed as food or cosmetics. Re-routing to drug framework or referral.

rules.name: Incomplete or Contradictory Formulation Facts
rules.condition: ingredients_classical_status == 'unknown' or administration_route == 'unknown' or intended_use == 'other' or (formulation_source == 'exact_classical_recipe' and classical_book_citation == null)

outcome.legal_basis: Master Plan Safety & Abstention Protocol; Drugs Rules Rule 158-B
outcome.explanation: Critical formulation facts missing or unverified. Missing classical treatise citation cannot be assumed proprietary. Issuing targeted missing-fact prompt and generating preliminary referral packet.
